title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integrations, Escalations, Health Checks & QBR Playbook (v2)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook captures the standardized process and artifacts Customer Success (CS) uses to onboard enterprise customers at Redwood Inference. It combines: (1) pre-sales handoff and integration checklists, (2) an escalation and incident routing playbook, (3) integration guidance and common patterns, (4) known issues and workarounds, and (5) health-check and QBR materials. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-success, ensure predictable handoffs, and provide a clear, auditable escalation path for customer-impacting problems.

Scope

- Audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, SRE on-call, and Product/Eng stakeholders assigned to the customer.
- Applies to: All enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments and high-touch hosted customers with enterprise SLAs.
- Out of scope: Self-serve signups without enterprise billing/commit contracts.

Roles & Ownership

- Customer Success Manager (CSM): overall project owner for onboarding, schedules QBRs, drives customer readiness checklist.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical owner for integration, test plan, and deployment validation.
- Support Engineer (Tier 2): first-line for escalations requiring internal triage.
- Eng-SRE/Runtime Team: owner for production incidents, performance regressions, and capacity issues.
- Product Owner: responsible for roadmap items surfaced during onboarding.

Onboarding Phases & Checklist

1) Pre-sales Handoff (Week -1 to 0)
   - Deliverables: signed contract, security questionnaires, network requirements, KMS/HSM details.
   - CSM actions: schedule kickoff, share onboarding plan and contacts, create internal Slack channel.
   - SE actions: confirm model selection, estimate capacity, create integration playbook stub.

2) Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Agenda: introductions, scope/goals, success criteria, timeline, SSO/KMS/RBAC requirements.
   - Checklist: assign owners, confirm endpoints, create test account, provide API keys/credentials using secure vault.

3) Integration & Validation (Week 1-4)
   - Tasks: implement API calls, webhooks, auth flows; validate latency and throughput against agreed SLOs; execute sample prompt sets.
   - Deliverables: integration checklist complete, smoke-test results, security attestations.

4) Go-Live (Week 4-6)
   - Steps: cutover plan, monitoring enabled, alert thresholds validated, rollback plan documented.
   - Post-cutover validation: traffic ramp, error budget checks, first 48h on-call monitoring.

5) Post-Go-Live (30/60/90 day)
   - 30-day: adoption health review, initial QBR scheduling.
   - 60-day: performance tuning (batching/quantization recommendations), cost optimization review.
   - 90-day: finalize success metrics, transition support model to steady-state.

Integration Guide (high-level)

- Auth & Secrets:
  - Use customer-specific API keys stored in our vault. For Private deployments provide KMS/HSM endpoints and rotation schedule.
  - Example curl (hosted):
    curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model":"rwd-open-1", "input":"Hello"}'

- Endpoints & Regions:
  - Confirm region (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1). For Dedicated, use customer-specific endpoint documented in the onboarding repo.

- Rate limits & Quotas:
  - Default hosted: 300 requests/min per account; enterprise customers receive custom quotas documented in the work order. SE to request quota changes via the capacity portal.

- Webhooks & Eventing:
  - Provide webhook delivery retry policy: 5 attempts, exponential backoff (1m, 2m, 4m, 8m, 16m). Document expected payload (JSON schema) in the integration artifact.

- Common Integration Patterns:
  - Proxying through backend service for key management and prompt orchestration.
  - Streaming responses to support low-latency UIs.
  - Prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes.

Escalation Playbook

Severity Definitions
- Sev 1 (Critical): Complete service outage for customer or sustained errors preventing production usage. Target initial response: 15 minutes.
- Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation in latency or partial feature failure affecting >10% requests. Target initial response: 1 hour.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Functional but degraded; impacts non-critical flows. Target initial response: 4 business hours.
- Sev 4 (Low): Informational, feature requests, or minor UI issues. Target response: 2 business days.

Routing Matrix
- Customer reports issue -> CSM triages -> Support Engineer (Tier 2) -> If root cause likely infra/runtime -> Eng-SRE -> If code bug/model issue -> Eng Serving Runtime/Product -> Escalate to Engineering on-call per SLA.

Escalation Steps (Sev1 example)
1) CSM acknowledges customer and opens internal incident channel.
2) Support Engineer verifies customer logs, request IDs, and reproducer.
3) Engage Eng-SRE on-call and attach runbook link.
4) If service degradation, trigger capacity rebalancing or fallback to compatible model variants.
5) Communicate cadence to customer every 30 minutes until resolution.
6) Post-incident: run a postmortem within 72 hours; include action items, owners, and ETA.

Communication & SLAs
- For Sev1/2 incidents, CSM to provide status updates every 30-60 minutes until severity lowered.
- For enterprise SLAs include agreed Mean Time to Acknowledge (MTTA) and Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR) in the contract; ensure Support team has routing configured.

Known Issues & Workarounds (selection)

| Issue | Symptoms | Workaround | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intermittent 503s on dedicated endpoints during autoscaling | 5-10% 503 for short bursts | Temporarily route to regional fallback endpoint; increase pool size and adjust scale-in delay | Eng-SRE |
| Tokenization mismatch for custom tokenizer builds | Generated outputs contain invalid tokens in edge cases | Use canonical tokenizer provided in model bundle; run tokenization unit tests before deploy | SE/Serving Runtime |
| Webhook delivery failure for private networks | Webhook timeouts reported | Provide customer with a retry endpoint and recommend static egress IPs or allowlist Redwood webhook IPs | Support/Networking |

Health Checks & QBR Materials

- Suggested onboarding health metrics (track weekly):
  - API success rate (%), 99.9% target for enterprise SLAs.
  - Median p95 latency (ms) and distribution by endpoint.
  - Token consumption vs committed quota.
  - Error budget burn rate.
  - Integration test pass rate.

- QBR Template (30-60 min):
  1) Executive summary: adoption & value delivered.
  2) Health dashboard: key metrics and recent incidents.
  3) Performance & cost: tokens, batching, and quantization recommendations.
  4) Roadmap & feature asks: prioritized backlog items.
  5) Next steps & action items.

Artifacts & Templates
- Onboarding checklist (CSV): fields for contact, endpoints, security items, test plan, and success criteria.
- Email templates: Kickoff, Go-Live confirmation, Post-Incident update.
- QBR slide deck template (link to internal template repository).

Runbooks & Links
- Primary runbook for Sev1 incidents: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/sev1-incident-playbook
- Integration API reference: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples
- Capacity change requests: cloud-accounts-and-networking/capacity-portal (internal)

Postmortem & Continuous Improvement
- For every Sev1/2 incident during onboarding, produce a short postmortem within 72 hours. Include customer impact, timeline, root cause, and at least one action with an owner. Review improvements in the next QBR.

Appendix: Quick Checklists
- Pre-kickoff: contract signed, contacts, security questionnaire complete.
- Before go-live: monitoring dashboards created, runbooks assigned, rollback plan verified.
- 90-day review: adoption targets met, cost optimization executed, handoff to steady-state support.

If you have questions about any step in this playbook or need the onboarding artifact templates, contact the Enterprise Onboarding mailbox (enterprise-onboarding@redwood.ai) or the CS internal channel in Slack.
